headline: High: shared filesystem and broad shell/network on transformers create default data-leakage and capability-conflict risks with Superset’s allowlisted egress.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Superset exposes a Superset API and allowlisted network egress, while transformers can read/write the filesystem, run browsers, and spawn subprocesses. A shared workspace or file handoff would let attacker-controlled content from one agent influence the other, but no direct shared channel is documented, so I choose medium over low due to uncertainty escalation.
conditions: IF the two agents exchange files through a shared workspace or copied artifacts, prompt injection becomes reachable.
IF transformers parses Superset-generated text as instructions, attacker-controlled content can steer tool use.
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent.
Disable automatic parsing of peer output as instructions.
Require human review before any cross-agent file handoff.
Strip markup and prompts from exchanged text.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Superset touches no declared secrets, but transformers reads files, runs browsers, and has broad egress, so any shared workspace can leak file contents to external services. Superset’s allowlisted egress reduces but does not eliminate exposure. Because the shared-storage pathway is plausible but undocumented, medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF both agents share a filesystem or mounted workspace, transformers can read Superset artifacts.
IF transformers sends those artifacts to remote inference or the Hugging Face Hub, leakage occurs.
mitigations: Use separate directories with OS permissions.
Avoid placing sensitive files in the shared workspace.
Disable outbound network for transformers during review runs.
Review browser and Hub access before execution.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Superset can call APIs and transformers can write the filesystem, execute shells, install packages, and spawn subprocesses. If they operate on the same directory or mutable project state, concurrent writes and side effects can collide. The profiles do not show locking or isolation, so the default-risk assessment is high.
conditions: IF both agents target the same filesystem path, write conflicts are possible.
IF transformers installs packages or spawns subprocesses while Superset is active, shared-state corruption can occur.
mitigations: Assign distinct working directories.
Run only one writer at a time.
Freeze package installation during shared runs.
Use read-only mounts for Superset inputs.
requires-engineering: add file locks around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Superset can produce analytics outputs via its API, and transformers can consume files and run subprocesses, so B may treat A’s output as authoritative without verification. No explicit validation step is documented, but no direct action-taking authority is shown either, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF transformers ingests Superset-generated reports without validation, errors can cascade.
IF downstream scripts act on those outputs, the cascade can affect multiple work products.
mitigations: Add a verification step before reuse.
Require source citations for any extracted facts.
Compare outputs against original inputs.
Limit downstream automation from B’s outputs.
requires-engineering: implement confidence gating on A-to-B handoffs.

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, residency, or retention mismatch is documented in either profile, and both are open-source with no declared secrets handled. The only compliance-relevant signal is transformers’ broad egress and file access, which could matter if regulated data is introduced, but that pathway is not established here. I therefore rate this low.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into transformers’ filesystem inputs, compliance review is required.
IF a residency or retention policy is imposed externally, the pair must be configured to match it.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared workspace.
Confirm retention settings before use.
Restrict outbound network destinations.
Document data-handling responsibilities.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention.
